description: Ground-truth question set for evals/fidelity-benchmark.sh. Reuses the same fixture files/groupings as evals/benchmarks.json (evals/fixtures/echo, real Go source from labstack/echo v5.3.1, MIT). Each ground_truth.must_mention list was extracted mechanically (grep) from the fixture files, not written from memory, so it can be re-derived and checked instead of trusted blindly. `adversarial: true` marks questions picked because a summarizing delegate is likely to drop or flatten at least one item (mixed naming conventions, less-common identifiers, entries defined far from the file's main cluster).
scoring: For each answer text, compute recall = (must_mention items found as a case-insensitive substring) / (total must_mention items). This is exact/structured matching, not LLM-judged.
hallucination_check: An item counts as an unsupported claim if it appears in the final answer (the one produced after Claude is given only the delegate's bulk-read answer, not the file) but does not appear anywhere in the delegate's own raw bulk-read answer. This is a heuristic, not proof of fabrication: Claude could paraphrase a delegate claim using different wording and trip a false positive. Treat unsupported_claims as a signal to inspect manually, not a final verdict.

questions.name: echo-http-methods
questions.question: List every HTTP method name for which the Echo type has a dedicated routing method (e.g. the method exists as `func (e *Echo) <NAME>(...)`), using the exact method name as it appears in the Go source.
questions.adversarial_reason: 10 methods exist, not just the common 4 (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE). CONNECT, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, QUERY, and TRACE are easy to drop in a summary.

questions.name: echo-wrap-functions
questions.question: What are the names of the two package-level functions used to wrap an existing net/http Handler or middleware function into Echo's own handler/middleware types?

questions.name: cors-config-fields
questions.question: What configuration options (struct field names) does the CORS middleware in the first file support, and which of them are exercised by the tests in the second file?

questions.name: cors-test-function-names
questions.question: List the exact names of every Go test function defined in the second file.
questions.adversarial_reason: Naming is inconsistent (TestCORS, TestCORSConfig, TestCORSWithConfig_AllowMethods, TestCorsHeaders vs Test_allowOriginScheme, Test_allowOriginFunc); the underscore-prefixed ones are easy to normalize away or drop in a summary.

questions.name: cross-file-exported-types
questions.question: Which exported (capitalized) top-level types are defined in each of these three files?
questions.adversarial_reason: router.go alone defines 7 exported types, three of which (AddRouteError, PathValues, PathValue) are defined far below the file's main cluster (Router/Routes/DefaultRouter/RouterConfig) and are easy to miss when skimming/summarizing a long file.
